Lucía: ¿Y la inversión? ¿Puede perder capital?
Asesor Mauro: Sí. Una inversión tiene riesgo y volatilidad, así que el capital invertido puede bajar. Por eso importa el horizonte de inversión.
Lucía: ¿Cuánto puedo perder en esta inversión? Necesito acceso al dinero en un año.
Asesor Mauro: No hay una cifra fija. La pérdida posible depende del producto, y un rendimiento potencial no es una garantía.
Lucía: Entonces el ahorro es para algo que necesito pronto, y la inversión sería para un plazo más largo.
Lucía anota sus dos metas: una cuenta de ahorros para el año, y una inversión solo si su horizonte lo permite.

25.speaking: Explica a un asesor qué parte de tu dinero quieres mantener en ahorro y qué parte, si alguna, podrías invertir. Pregunta cuánto podrías perder y cómo funciona el acceso. Termina diciendo qué dinero mantendrás disponible y qué te falta investigar.
25.openingLine: Good afternoon. What would you like to compare between saving and investing?

examples.es: The possible loss depends on the product.

examples.es: The invested capital can go down.

reading.title: Shares, bonds and funds
target: Ivan studies a fictional brochure with three products: a share, a bond, and an investment fund.
Ivan: What does this share represent? Does it give me a part of the company?
Adviser Gina: Yes, a share represents a part of the company, and it can pay dividends if the company decides to pay them.
Ivan: And the bond? Who is the issuer of the bond?
Adviser Gina: The issuer is the one who borrows money. The bond has a maturity date and may pay coupons on fixed dates.
Ivan: And the fund? What is the management fee?
Adviser Gina: A fund pools money from many people and buys a portfolio of assets. This fictional fund charges a management fee of 1.2% a year.
Ivan: Diversification reduces the risk of a single asset, right? But there is no guaranteed return.
Adviser Gina: Correct. Before you choose, ask what each product represents, who issues it, and how much it costs to hold.

reading.title: Fund costs and diversification
target: Renata compares two fictional funds and wants to know what they really cost.
Renata: How much does this fund cost each year? I want the full number.
Adviser Leo: The management fee is 0.85% a year, and the total annual expense, with other fund costs, is 1.10%.
Renata: Is there an entry or exit charge? And is there a transaction fee?
Adviser Leo: The entry charge is taken when you buy, and the exit charge when you sell. This fund has neither, but it charges $5.00 per transaction.
Renata: Does the fund have a diversified portfolio, or does it concentrate everything in a few assets?
Adviser Leo: Holding several assets does not remove the risk, but it reduces the concentration in a single company.
Renata: What happens if I put everything into one share? And is a stock index fund diversified?
Adviser Leo: With a single share, everything depends on one company. An index fund spreads the money across many companies, but it stays in one asset class, and its value can fall.

Renata: ¿Hay un cargo de entrada o de salida? ¿Y hay una comisión por transacción?
Asesor Leo: El cargo de entrada se cobra al comprar, y el de salida al vender. Este fondo no tiene ninguno de los dos, pero cobra $5.00 por transacción.
Renata: ¿El fondo tiene un portafolio diversificado, o concentra todo en pocos activos?
Asesor Leo: Tener varios activos no elimina el riesgo, pero sí reduce la concentración en una sola empresa.

Asesor Leo: Con una sola acción, todo depende de una empresa. Un fondo indexado reparte el dinero entre muchas empresas, pero sigue en una sola clase de activo y su valor puede bajar.

reading.title: A 401(k) plan in the United States
target: Samuel works in the United States for a fictional company that offers a 401(k) plan, a workplace retirement account.
Samuel: How much does my employer contribute? And how much do I contribute?

Adviser Tania: You choose your personal contribution, within the annual limit that the IRS sets each year.
Samuel: What is the retirement age in the plan, and when can I use the money?

Adviser Tania: It depends on the plan and on the reason for the withdrawal. The tax benefit also depends on the type of contribution, traditional or Roth.

reading.title: An ATM with a cash shortage
target: Mark withdraws cash from the ATM at his neighborhood branch on a Saturday afternoon.
The screen shows that the withdrawal was successful, and the receipt shows the requested amount of $300.00.
Mark: I requested $300.00, but I received $200.00. One hundred-dollar bill is missing.
Mark: What is the procedure for a shortage? Can you review the transaction log?
Operator Nadia: Yes. I will review the transaction log and the cash balancing for that machine.
Operator Nadia: The cash dispenser reported a damaged bill, and the machine returned it inside.
Operator Nadia: The preliminary count shows $100.00 extra in the machine, but the official cash balancing is done on Monday.
Mark: So the machine did not give out all of the cash, even though the screen said everything was fine.
Operator Nadia: You can file a complaint and ask for an investigation with the security camera in the branch.
Mark: I want to file a formal complaint. How long does the investigation take?
Operator Nadia: The investigation usually takes several business days, and we will give you a case number.
Mark writes down the case number and keeps the printed receipt.
Mark leaves the branch with the receipt and the case number, and he will call again if he has no answer after the Monday balancing.

reading.title: A transfer that has been delayed
target: Gabriela sent an international transfer of $850.00 to her sister four days ago, and the deposit still does not appear.

Agent Ruiz: What is the transfer reference? Let's also check the receiving bank you chose.
Gabriela: The reference is on my sending receipt: TRF 20931.
Agent Ruiz: The reference matches, but the bank code of the destination has a different digit.
Gabriela: Does that mean there was a rejection?
Agent Ruiz: There is no rejection yet. The payment instruction is on hold until you confirm the correct code.
Gabriela: My sister has just sent me the correct code by text message. I will confirm it now.
Agent Ruiz: Thank you. With the corrected code, the receiving bank is processing the instruction again.
Gabriela: What is the processing time of the receiving bank? How many business days does crediting take?
Agent Ruiz: It is normally three business days, so the crediting date will be Thursday.
Gabriela: Can you trace the payment instruction from your system? I want a trace.
Agent Ruiz: Yes. I have recorded the trace with the case number. If the receiving bank cannot apply the payment, the money comes back to your account as a return.
Gabriela: I need the sending receipt for my complaint, so I am keeping it as proof.
Agent Ruiz: I recommend not sending another transfer until the bank confirms the crediting date.
Gabriela writes down the reference, and on Thursday she asks her sister whether the deposit has arrived.

reading.title: A charge that appears twice
target: Tomas checks his transaction history: there are two charges from the same merchant for $65.00 each.
Tomas: There are two charges from the same merchant. Is this a temporary authorization or a posted charge? I only bought once.
Adviser Irene: First, let's check the status of each one. A temporary authorization appears as pending and is released if the merchant does not confirm it.
Tomas: Is it possible that the second charge is a temporary authorization that has not been released yet?
Adviser Irene: Not in this case. Both have a settlement date of November 3, so both are posted charges.
Adviser Irene: They also have different authorization numbers, which shows that the merchant sent the purchase twice.
Tomas: I need the bank to review the repeated charge. The store receipt shows a single purchase of $65.00.
Adviser Irene: There is a complication: the merchant sent a correction notice, but the charge reversal still does not appear.
Tomas: When will the correction be made? Can you give me the authorization number of the second charge?
Adviser Irene: It is 448120. If the merchant does not make the reversal within ten business days, the bank can process a duplicate-charge claim.
Tomas: I want the reversal to appear on my statement before the end of this month.
Adviser Irene: It may appear sooner, but I cannot promise the date. I am opening the case today with your receipt and the date of each charge.
Tomas: Then I want you to record my complaint today. I am keeping the merchant notice as proof.
Tomas marks the duplicate charge on his sheet and checks his history every week until he sees the correction.

reading.title: An activity I do not recognize
target: Hannah receives a notice from her bank about a login from an unknown device.
Hannah: There is a login that I do not recognize. I am worried that someone is using my account, and I did not make any transfer this week.
Specialist Omar: Thank you for reporting it. We will review the unusual activity on your account.

Specialist Omar: Then there may have been unauthorized access. Let's check the unknown device in the access list.
Hannah: Can you apply a precautionary block to my account? I want to prevent transactions that I did not make.
Specialist Omar: Yes, I can apply it. First, please confirm that you called us at the official number shown in the app or on your card.
Hannah: Yes, I called the number in the app. I will use only the official contact of the bank, not links in emails.
Specialist Omar: Very well. I will ask you for an identity check in the app, and then we will review the logins.
Hannah: What steps should I follow to protect my account? Can you turn on a security alert?
Specialist Omar: Yes. I will activate a security alert and reduce the transaction limit to $200.00 while we review the case.
Specialist Omar: There is a complication: with the precautionary block, your automatic rent payment tomorrow will not go out.
Hannah: Then I will keep the block and pay the rent at the branch. I want the unknown device removed from my list today.
Specialist Omar: I have already removed it. You will receive a confirmation email with the activity report and your case number.

Especialista Omar: Muy bien. Le pediré una verificación de identidad en la app, y después revisaremos los inicios de sesión.
Hannah: ¿Qué pasos debo seguir para proteger mi cuenta? ¿Puede activar una alerta de seguridad?
Especialista Omar: Sí. Activaré una alerta de seguridad y reduciré el límite de transacciones a $200.00 mientras revisamos el caso.
Especialista Omar: Hay una complicación: con el bloqueo preventivo, el pago automático de su renta de mañana no saldrá.

reading.title: A message that asks for money urgently
target: Elisa receives an urgent message that appears to come from her bank and asks for an emergency transfer.
Elisa calls the official number printed on her card, not the number in the message.
Elisa: The message says there is a threat of closure if I do not send $900.00 today.
Elisa: Who is the sender of this message? It looks official, and it has my full name and the last four digits of my card.
Adviser Lupe: That information can come from another source; it does not prove that the sender is the bank. This looks like a scam.
Elisa: The message includes a link with the bank logo and asks for a verification code.
Adviser Lupe: It is a fake link and identity impersonation. Never share a verification code with anyone.
Adviser Lupe: Your bank does not ask for an urgent payment or an emergency transfer by text message.
Elisa: Can you verify this request through the official number? I want to confirm that my account has no problem.
Adviser Lupe: Confirmed: there is no payment request and no threat of closure on your account.
Elisa: There is another complication: while we are talking, a second message has arrived. It says I have ten minutes.
Adviser Lupe: The urgency is part of the scam. Do not open the link; I can mark both messages as suspicious in your file.
Adviser Lupe: If someone calls you on behalf of the bank, confirm it with the trusted contact: this official number or your branch.
Elisa: Thank you. I called the number on my card, and this number is my verified channel. I want to report the sender to the security team.
Elisa takes a screenshot for the report, deletes the messages without opening the link, and writes down the time of each one.

Elisa llama al número oficial que aparece en su tarjeta, no al número del mensaje.

Elisa: El mensaje incluye un enlace con el logotipo del banco y pide un código de verificación.
Asesora Lupe: Es un enlace falso y una suplantación de identidad. Nunca comparta un código de verificación con nadie.
Asesora Lupe: Su banco no pide un pago urgente ni una transferencia de emergencia por mensaje de texto.
Elisa: ¿Puede verificar esta solicitud por el número oficial? Quiero confirmar que mi cuenta no tiene ningún problema.
Asesora Lupe: Confirmado: no hay ninguna solicitud de pago ni amenaza de cierre en su cuenta.

Asesora Lupe: Si alguien la llama en nombre del banco, confírmelo con el contacto de confianza: este número oficial o su sucursal.
Elisa: Gracias. Llamé al número de mi tarjeta, y este número es mi canal verificado. Quiero reportar al remitente ante el equipo de seguridad.
Elisa toma una captura de pantalla para el reporte, borra los mensajes sin abrir el enlace y anota la hora de cada uno.

reading.title: A promise of investment return
target: Bruno attends a sales presentation for a fictional fund that promises a guaranteed return of 20% a year.
Bruno: What is the basis for that promise? If the return is safe, why does nobody else do it?
Salesperson Gabriel: Our team has a very effective strategy, and the past results are excellent.
Bruno: Past results guarantee nothing. What risk does this product carry? And what happens with the possible loss if the market falls?
Salesperson Gabriel: The risk is low because we have a guaranteed return, so there is no possible loss.
Bruno: How much are the fees? I want to see the full table before I sign the investment contract.
Salesperson Gabriel: The fees are minimal, and there is an exit penalty only if you withdraw in the first year.
Bruno: Can I withdraw my money when I need it? I need access to the money in six months.
Salesperson Gabriel: That is your decision, but it is better to invest today so you do not miss the opportunity.
Bruno: I prefer to read the full prospectus and review my investment horizon before I decide.
Salesperson Gabriel: You can pay today by transfer, and the opportunity closes tomorrow.
Bruno: I need the money in six months, so I sign nothing today. No written promise by itself proves there is no risk.
Bruno: Before I decide, I also ask whether the fund is registered with the securities regulator in its country.
Bruno leaves with the prospectus and a list of questions about risk, fees, access to money and registration.

Bruno: Los resultados anteriores no garantizan nada. ¿Qué riesgo tiene este producto? ¿Y qué pasa con la pérdida posible si el mercado cae?

reading.title: A sudden change in income
target: Daniela calls her bank because this month's payroll deposit did not reach her account.
Daniela: My paycheck stopped arriving after the last pay period. Since when has the payment been suspended?
Officer Javier: The last deposit from your employer was on the 3rd. Since then there has been no new payment, neither suspended nor rejected.
Daniela: Can you explain why the payment was suspended?
Officer Javier: The bank does not see a rejection: the employer has not sent the payment yet. Your employer has to give that explanation.
Daniela: Human resources told me this morning that my contract ended. I no longer receive the monthly income of $2,400.00.
Officer Javier: I am sorry. Check your charge account, because your automatic payments may be rejected if the balance is not enough.
Officer Javier: If a loan installment is due soon, you can ask the loan department for a payment plan.
Officer Javier: Your emergency reserve has $3,600.00 available in the savings account.
Daniela: Nico, my pay has stopped and my contract ended. We need a budget review tonight.
Nico: This changes our plan for the coming months. Without your income, only my $1,500.00 a month comes in.
Daniela: How long can we use the emergency reserve? The essential expenses are $2,700.00 a month.
Nico: We are short $1,200.00 every month, so the $3,600.00 reserve covers three months.
Daniela: First the rent payment and the loan installment. We cut non-essential spending and ask for a payment plan if we need one.
Nico: Agreed. Meanwhile, we use the charge account only for essentials, and we confirm the payday of your last paycheck.

Ejecutivo Javier: Si una cuota del préstamo vence pronto, puede pedir un plan de pagos al área de préstamos.
Ejecutivo Javier: Su reserva de emergencia tiene $3,600.00 disponibles en la cuenta de ahorros.

reading.title: Asking for an arrangement on a late payment
target: Monica calls the service center of her internet provider because she is having trouble paying this month.
Monica: I am having trouble making the payment this month. I want to explain my situation before it falls further behind.
Agent Ernesto: I understand. I see an overdue balance of $74.00 and a delinquency status since last week.
Monica: What arrangements do you offer for a late payment? My account was up to date before last month.
Agent Ernesto: We can offer a partial payment today and a payment agreement for the rest.
Monica: Can you give me a two-week deferral? And how much is the late charge?
Agent Ernesto: There is a complication: because the account is already delinquent, I cannot give you a deferral. Without a payment within five days, the service is suspended.
Agent Ernesto: If you pay $40.00 today, the $10.00 late charge does not apply, and the remaining $34.00 goes into a payment agreement.
Monica: I want to sign a payment agreement. Can you help me with a recovery plan?
Agent Ernesto: The recovery plan splits the $34.00 into two payments of $17.00, added to your bills for the next two months.
Monica: Could I get a temporary reduction of the monthly fee? My income returns to normal in February.
Agent Ernesto: Yes, I can apply an installment adjustment: a basic plan for two months, at $35.00 instead of $45.00.
Monica: I can pay part of it today. Could you also send me a commitment letter with the dates?
Agent Ernesto: Yes. The commitment letter appears in your account, and your new due date is December 20.
Monica writes down the $40.00 partial payment, the new due date, and the agent's name before she ends the call.

reading.title: Reviewing a consolidation proposal
target: Andrew reviews a debt consolidation proposal from a fictional lender.
Andrew: My total debt adds up to $6,000.00. What is the repayment proposal, and what does it include?
Adviser Sofia: The monthly payment in the proposal is $176.25 for 48 months, with a fixed annual interest rate of 18%.
Andrew: What is the total cost of this proposal? How much is the total interest?
Adviser Sofia: It is $8,460.00 in payments, so the total interest is $2,460.00.
Adviser Sofia: There is a complication: the $120.00 opening fee is deducted from the loan, so you receive $5,880.00.
Andrew: Then I am $120.00 short of paying off all my debts. How much does the monthly payment fall with a longer term?
Adviser Sofia: With 60 months, the payment falls to $152.36, but the total interest rises to $3,141.60.
Adviser Sofia: With 36 months, the payment rises to $216.91, but the interest falls to $1,808.76.
Andrew: I want to see the full payment schedule, with the amortization of each installment.
Adviser Sofia: In the schedule, most of each early payment is interest, and the balance to clear falls slowly.
Andrew: What is the final payment? Is any balance left at the end of the full term?
Adviser Sofia: The final payment may differ by a few cents because of rounding, and then the balance is zero. There is no penalty for early payment.
Andrew: I will compare the total debt with my current plan before I sign anything.
Andrew saves the proposal and schedules a review with Sofia for next week.

Andrés: ¿Cuál es el costo total de esta propuesta? ¿Cuánto son los intereses totales?
Asesora Sofía: Son $8,460.00 en pagos, así que los intereses totales son $2,460.00.
Asesora Sofía: Hay una complicación: la comisión de apertura de $120.00 se descuenta del préstamo, así que usted recibe $5,880.00.

Asesora Sofía: Con 36 meses, el pago sube a $216.91, pero los intereses bajan a $1,808.76.

reading.title: A shared household budget
target: Paula and Ivan review the shared budget for their home before they sign the new rental contract.
Paula: I earn $2,400.00 and you earn $1,800.00. How do we split the shared expenses?
Ivan: I propose that each of us contributes according to income. What percentage does each of us pay?
Paula: With those incomes, I would pay 57% and you would pay 43%, so the proportion is clear.
Ivan: Agreed. The rent is $1,200.00, so I contribute $516.00 and you contribute $684.00.
Paula: We can use a joint account for the rent and the electricity bill, and each of us keeps a personal account.
Ivan: Who pays the electricity bill this month? We can do it with the shared balance.
Paula: Yes, it comes out of the joint account, so the split stays balanced in the same proportion.
Ivan: There is an unexpected expense: the garage says the car repair costs $450.00 in parts.
Paula: How much is the unexpected expense in total, including labor?
Ivan: With labor it is $600.00, and the common fund only has $400.00.
Paula: We can use the common fund for the repair and split the other $200.00 by the proportion: I put in $114.00 and you put in $86.00.
Ivan: Agreed. Afterward we replenish the fund with the monthly contribution. Let's make an agreement in writing.
Paula and Ivan write down the proportion, the shared balance, and the date of the next monthly review.

Paula e Iván anotan la proporción, el saldo compartido y la fecha de la próxima revisión mensual.

reading.title: A limit with a family member
target: Julian receives a call from his cousin Ramiro, who wants a personal loan to pay off a debt.
Ramiro: Can you lend me $800.00 for two months? I will pay everything back, I promise.
Julian: I am sorry, but I cannot lend you money this month. I have a financial limit that I respect.
Ramiro: It is a small thing, and we are family. Can you be my co-signer?
Julian: I prefer not to be your co-signer, because it is a financial commitment I cannot take on.
Ramiro: I will pay it back in two months; that would be the repayment date. Not even a little?
Julian: I can help you with a payment plan for your debt, but not with borrowed money from my account.
Julian: If it helps, I can give you some financial help, $50.00, as a gift and not as a loan.
Ramiro: I thought we had a relationship of trust.
Julian: We do, and that is why I prefer to tell you the truth. It is a personal decision that I respect.
Ramiro: All right. How do we handle the debt payment in practice?
Julian: Let's make a list of your payments on Saturday. I will review the family budget with my wife next month.
Julian ends the call and writes down his financial boundary and his savings plan, and does not feel guilty about saying it.

Ramiro: Pensé que teníamos una relación de confianza.
Julián: La tenemos, y por eso prefiero decirte la verdad. Es una decisión personal que respeto.

Julián termina la llamada, anota su límite financiero y su plan de ahorro, y no se siente culpable por decirlo.

reading.title: Reviewing fees before a closure
target: Mariana wants to close her current account and move her money to another bank before she moves to another city.
Mariana: How much does it cost to close this account? I want to know if there is a closing fee.
Adviser Ricardo: There is a closing fee of $25.00 if the account has been open for less than six months.
Mariana: I opened the account five months ago. If I wait a few weeks, do I avoid the fee?
Adviser Ricardo: Exactly. After the 15th of next month, the account closure has no fee.
Mariana: What happens to my direct debits? I have three monthly charges on that account.
Adviser Ricardo: Before closing it, you must move the direct debits to the new account; otherwise those charges will be rejected after the closure.
Mariana: And the outstanding checks? I have a check that has not been cashed yet.
Adviser Ricardo: Under our policy, outstanding checks must be cashed before the closure, and there can be no pending charges.
Mariana: What is the closing period? Does the linked card stay active afterward?
Adviser Ricardo: The closure takes up to ten business days. The linked card will be blocked when the closure is confirmed.
Mariana: Is there a grace period to use the card? Is there a transfer fee?
Adviser Ricardo: There is no grace period, but moving the final balance has no fee if the new bank requests it.
Mariana: Then I will make a balance transfer to the new account. When does the balance transfer happen?
Adviser Ricardo: It happens when the closure is confirmed. Request a closure confirmation in writing and check that no pending charge is left.
Mariana writes down the deadlines, saves the closure confirmation, and schedules a check of the final balance for next week.

Mariana: ¿Cuánto cuesta cerrar esta cuenta? Quiero saber si hay una comisión por cierre.

Mariana: Abrí la cuenta hace cinco meses. Si espero unas semanas, ¿no pago la comisión?

reading.title: A decline in a fictional portfolio
target: Ana checks her fictional portfolio after a market decline that lasted several weeks.
Ana: My portfolio fell 8% this month, from $10,000.00 to $9,200.00. What does that mean?
Educator Teresa: It means the portfolio value fell by $800.00, but it is an unrealized loss.
Ana: Is that loss real, or is it only on paper?
Educator Teresa: It is called an unrealized loss because you have not sold yet, but the current value really has fallen. We do not know whether it will recover.
Ana: Why did it fall so much? I saw on the news that the market is falling, and I thought about a panic sale.
Educator Teresa: Fluctuation and volatility are normal: the investment price keeps going up and down every day.
Ana: What is my investment plan for this case? My investment horizon is ten years.
Educator Teresa: The useful question is whether your goal or your horizon has changed, not just this week's price.
Ana: Past performance does not guarantee the future, right? Should I rebalance the portfolio?
Educator Teresa: Rebalancing means returning to the percentages in your plan. It can adjust the risk, but it does not guarantee a recovery.
Ana: Is there always a rebound after a decline?
Educator Teresa: A rebound can happen, but nobody knows when. The value can stay low even if you do not sell; selling realizes the loss.
Ana: I am not going to sell in a panic. I am writing my investment plan tonight.
native: Ana revisa su cartera ficticia después de una caída del mercado que duró varias semanas.
Ana: Mi cartera bajó un 8% este mes, de $10,000.00 a $9,200.00. ¿Qué significa?
Educadora Teresa: Significa que el valor de la cartera bajó $800.00, pero es una pérdida no realizada.
Ana: ¿Esa pérdida ya es real o solo está en el papel?
Educadora Teresa: Se llama pérdida no realizada porque aún no ha vendido, pero el valor actual sí bajó. No sabemos si se recuperará.
Ana: ¿Por qué bajó tanto? Vi en las noticias que el mercado está bajando y pensé en una venta en pánico.
Educadora Teresa: La fluctuación y la volatilidad son normales: el precio de la inversión sigue subiendo y bajando cada día.
Ana: ¿Cuál es mi plan de inversión para este caso? Mi horizonte de inversión es de diez años.
Educadora Teresa: La pregunta útil es si cambió su meta o su horizonte, no solo el precio de esta semana.
Ana: El rendimiento pasado no garantiza el futuro, ¿verdad? ¿Debo reequilibrar la cartera?
Educadora Teresa: El reequilibrio consiste en volver a los porcentajes de su plan. Puede ajustar el riesgo, pero no garantiza una recuperación.
Ana: ¿Siempre hay un rebote después de una caída?
Educadora Teresa: Puede haber un rebote, pero nadie sabe cuándo. El valor puede seguir bajo aunque no venda; al vender, la pérdida se realiza.
Ana: No voy a vender en pánico. Escribo mi plan de inversión esta noche.

Separa el movimiento del precio de una pérdida realizada, di tu horizonte de inversión y explica que una caída no es un resultado garantizado. Termina diciendo qué revisarás en tu plan y qué no harás por pánico.
14.openingLine: Good afternoon. I see your fictional portfolio fell this month. What worries you most?

reading.title: Two goals with different time frames
target: Lorena has two goals with different time frames: paying her son's university tuition and saving for her retirement.
Lorena: My short-term goal is the tuition: I need $12,000.00 in two years.
Educator Samuel: Then there is a liquidity need in your short horizon: that money has to be available on a fixed date.
Lorena: Can I have a liquidity reserve and also invest? My long-term goal is my retirement, twenty years from now.
Educator Samuel: You can have both the reserve and the investment, although separate goals do not always require separate accounts.
Lorena: The bank offers me a two-year fixed-term investment for the tuition. What happens if I need a partial withdrawal?
Educator Samuel: There is a complication: the university wants the first payment in eighteen months, and a partial withdrawal before the term ends may carry a penalty.
Lorena: Then I have a conflict between two time frames, and also one inside the tuition goal.
Educator Samuel: For retirement, you can set up a scheduled contribution each month and adjust the amount to your income.
Lorena: What is the best option for my long horizon?
Educator Samuel: I cannot tell you that; you would discuss it with an investment adviser. A diversified investment can go up or down, and nobody guarantees a result.
Lorena: I want to prepare a list of questions for the investment adviser before the next appointment.
Educator Samuel: Good idea. Include the time frame of each goal, the partial withdrawal penalty, and the costs of each product.
Lorena writes down her two goals, sets the tuition money apart, and schedules the next review.

Lorena: ¿Puedo tener una reserva de liquidez y también invertir? Mi meta a largo plazo es mi jubilación, dentro de veinte años.

reading.title: Comparing two car financing offers
target: Gustavo compares two financing offers for a car. The vehicle price is $18,000.00.
Gustavo: With a down payment of $3,000.00, what is the financed amount in the dealership offer?
Sales rep Hugo: The financed amount is $15,000.00, over 48 months, with a fixed annual rate of 11.5%.
Gustavo: What are the monthly payment and the total payments of the plan? I want to see the total cost.
Sales rep Hugo: The monthly payment is $391.34, and the total of the 48 payments is $18,784.32.
Gustavo: My sister recommended a credit union with another offer: the same amount over 36 months at a fixed rate of 10.2%.
Gustavo: Is the required insurance included? I need to see the offer in writing.
Sales rep Hugo: The required insurance is paid separately with either offer, so it does not change the comparison.
Gustavo: Is the annual rate fixed or variable in your offer? This paper says variable rate after month 12.
Sales rep Hugo: You are right, I am sorry. It is a fixed rate for the first year and then a variable rate, so the payment can change.
Gustavo: Then I compare the total cost of each offer, not just the monthly payment. The credit union has a fixed rate for all 36 months.
Gustavo: At the credit union I would pay $485.42 a month, with total payments of $17,475.12: more per month, but less in total.
Sales rep Hugo: You can ask for the financing plan in writing, and the down payment is paid before delivery.
Gustavo saves both offers in his email and decides after talking to his sister.

reading.title: A benefit letter and an IRS notice
target: Teresa lives in Texas and receives two letters: one from a county housing support program, which is fictional, and a notice from the IRS.
Teresa: What kind of document is this? The notice says that my 2025 federal tax return has an income difference.
Operator Clara: It looks like an official document from the IRS, the federal tax authority. To confirm it, use the phone number on the official IRS website, not only the one in the letter.
Teresa: Is this letter from the tax authority? It has my tax number, but my declared income was lower than the income it mentions.
Operator Clara: The notice proposes a change; it is not a final decision. It states the deadline to respond and the official form you must fill out.
Teresa: What is the filing deadline for my response? And does the support program letter change because of this?
Operator Clara: The filing deadline is printed on the notice. Under the county program rules, your benefit payment may be recalculated with the declared income.
Teresa: Does this deduction apply to my federal return? I paid for a training course last year.
Operator Clara: I cannot confirm that by phone. A tax specialist must review your case with your receipts, for example at an IRS VITA center.
Teresa: I need a tax specialist for my case. Which documents do I need to take to the appointment?
Operator Clara: Bring the notice, the benefit letter, your 2025 return and the course receipts. Your reference number is 6142.
Teresa: And what if in the end there is a tax refund and not a debt?
Operator Clara: A refund or a deduction depends on the review; I cannot promise you a figure.
Teresa keeps both letters, writes down the filing deadline and the appointment with the specialist, and pays nothing before she verifies the notice.
native: Teresa vive en Texas y recibe dos cartas: una de un programa de apoyo de vivienda del condado, que es ficticio, y un aviso del IRS.

Operadora Clara: El aviso propone un cambio; no es una decisión final. Indica el plazo para responder y el formulario oficial que debe llenar.
Teresa: ¿Cuál es el plazo de presentación de mi respuesta? ¿Y la carta del programa de apoyo cambia por esto?

Operadora Clara: Un reembolso o una deducción depende de la revisión; no puedo prometerle una cifra.
Teresa guarda las dos cartas, anota el plazo de presentación y la cita con el especialista, y no paga nada antes de verificar el aviso.

reading.title: Accompanying a family member at the bank
target: Daniel goes with his mother to a branch in the United States to review an account in her name.
Daniel: I only give language assistance, because the forms are in English. My mother wants to do the procedure herself.
Teller Patricia: Good afternoon. Is Mrs. Carmen the account holder? I need the identification of the account holder.
Carmen: Yes, I am the account holder. My English is basic, so my son is my interpreter today.
Teller Patricia: I understand. If he signs anything for you, under the bank and state rules he needs a power of attorney or a written authorization.
Daniel: Do I need a written authorization to help my mother with the form?
Teller Patricia: To help with the language, no. I need the authorization form signed by your mother so that you can sign as an authorized person.
Carmen: I want to sign myself. Son, do not sign anything for me.
Teller Patricia: The signature of the account holder must match the identification, and any consent is recorded in the system.
Daniel: There is a complication: my mother signed a power of attorney in another state last year. Is it valid here?
Teller Patricia: The bank sends it for legal review. It may take five business days, and meanwhile you cannot sign for her.
Daniel: What documents does the bank need for an authorized person? I want to prepare everything correctly.
Teller Patricia: If your mother does not have a legal representative, the account stays in her name, and you only accompany the procedure.
Daniel: So today I only help with the language, and she signs everything. If she wants to delegate, she will sign the authorization form.
Carmen: I want you to explain each step to me slowly, although I do the procedure myself.
native: Daniel acompaña a su madre a una sucursal en Estados Unidos para revisar una cuenta a nombre de ella.
Daniel: Yo solo le doy asistencia con el idioma, porque los formularios están en inglés. Mi madre quiere hacer el trámite ella misma.
Cajera Patricia: Buenas tardes. ¿La señora Carmen es la titular de la cuenta? Necesito la identificación del titular.
Carmen: Sí, soy la titular de la cuenta. Mi inglés es básico, así que mi hijo es mi intérprete hoy.
Cajera Patricia: Entiendo. Si él firma algo por usted, según las reglas del banco y del estado necesita un poder notarial o una autorización por escrito.
Daniel: ¿Necesito una autorización por escrito para ayudar a mi madre con el formulario?
Cajera Patricia: Para ayudar con el idioma, no. Necesito el formulario de autorización firmado por su madre para que usted pueda firmar como persona autorizada.
Carmen: Yo quiero firmar yo misma. Hijo, no firmes nada por mí.
Cajera Patricia: La firma del titular debe coincidir con la identificación, y cualquier consentimiento queda registrado en el sistema.
Daniel: Hay una complicación: mi madre firmó un poder notarial en otro estado el año pasado. ¿Sirve aquí?
Cajera Patricia: El banco lo envía a revisión legal. Puede tardar cinco días hábiles, y mientras tanto usted no puede firmar por ella.
Daniel: ¿Qué documentos necesita el banco para una persona autorizada? Quiero prepararlo todo bien.
Cajera Patricia: Si su madre no tiene un representante legal, la cuenta sigue a su nombre, y usted solo acompaña el trámite.
Daniel: Entonces hoy solo le ayudo con el idioma, y ella firma todo. Si quiere delegar, firmará el formulario de autorización.
Carmen: Quiero que usted me explique cada paso despacio, aunque el trámite lo hago yo.

18.speaking: Tu madre necesita ayuda en el banco. Explica que puedes ayudar con el idioma, pregunta si necesitas una autorización por escrito y qué documentos pide el banco para una persona autorizada. Termina diciendo quién firmará cada documento y qué hará ella misma.
18.openingLine: Good afternoon. Is the lady here for her own account, or are you coming with her?
18.partnerRole: Cajera de un banco que atiende en inglés en el mostrador

grammar.focus: So that + can expresa el propósito de una acción de otra persona (so that you can sign). En español se usa para que + subjuntivo; en inglés, so that + can o will.

examples.es: I need the form so that you can sign as an authorized person.
examples.en: Necesito el formulario para que usted pueda firmar como persona autorizada.

examples.es: I sign the form myself.
examples.en: Firmo el formulario yo misma.

reading.title: Explaining a purchase decision
target: Sebastian has to explain to his brother Mateo why he wants to buy a used car instead of waiting a year.
Mateo: Explain your financial decision to me in plain words, please.
Sebastian: My goal is to change cars without large debts: the used one costs $9,500.00 and I have $8,000.00. The alternative is to wait a year and save more.
Mateo: What is your main assumption? If income falls, what happens to the installments on the missing $1,500.00?
Sebastian: My main assumption is that income stays the same. If I wait, I keep paying for repairs on the old car: that is the opportunity cost of waiting.
Mateo: What is the main risk of this decision? And which scenario worries you the most?
Sebastian: The main risk is an expensive repair on the used car. In that scenario, I would have to use part of the emergency fund.
Mateo: Did you make a comparison with a new car? What decision deadline does the seller set?
Sebastian: Yes, I made a comparison of three options and an evaluation of the total cost. The decision deadline is this Friday.
Mateo: Is this a recommendation for the family or only your decision?
Sebastian: It is my decision, not a recommendation. My provisional conclusion is to buy the used car, but I still have an open question about the warranty.
Mateo: Then explain the alternative in one sentence, so that it is clear.
Sebastian: The alternative is to wait a year, save more, and buy with less debt, even if the car costs more.
Mateo listens calmly, asks two questions, and agrees to review the decision with Sebastian on Friday.
native: Sebastián tiene que explicar a su hermano Mateo por qué quiere comprar un auto usado en lugar de esperar un año.
Mateo: Explícame tu decisión financiera, pero en palabras sencillas, por favor.
Sebastián: Mi objetivo es cambiar de auto sin deudas grandes: el usado cuesta $9,500.00 y tengo $8,000.00. La alternativa es esperar un año y ahorrar más.
Mateo: ¿Cuál es tu supuesto principal? Si el ingreso baja, ¿qué pasa con las cuotas de los $1,500.00 que faltan?
Sebastián: Mi supuesto principal es que el ingreso se mantiene. Si espero, sigo pagando reparaciones del auto viejo: ese es el costo de oportunidad de esperar.
Mateo: ¿Cuál es el riesgo principal de esta decisión? ¿Y qué escenario te preocupa más?
Sebastián: El riesgo principal es una reparación costosa en el auto usado. En ese escenario, tendría que usar parte del fondo de emergencia.
Mateo: ¿Hiciste una comparación con un auto nuevo? ¿Cuál es el plazo de decisión que fija el vendedor?
Sebastián: Sí, hice una comparación de tres opciones y una evaluación del costo total. El plazo de decisión es este viernes.
Mateo: ¿Esto es una recomendación para la familia o solo tu decisión?
Sebastián: Es mi decisión, no una recomendación. Mi conclusión provisional es comprar el auto usado, pero todavía tengo una pregunta pendiente sobre la garantía.
Mateo: Entonces explícame la alternativa en una frase, para que quede clara.
Sebastián: La alternativa es esperar un año, ahorrar más y comprar con menos deuda, aunque el auto sea más caro.
Mateo escucha con calma, hace dos preguntas y acuerda revisar la decisión con Sebastián el viernes.

19.speaking: Explica a tu hermano la decisión de comprar un auto usado en lugar de esperar un año. Di tu meta, la alternativa, tu supuesto principal, el riesgo principal y la pregunta pendiente sobre la garantía. Termina con tu conclusión provisional y el día en que la revisarás.
19.openingLine: Explain your financial decision to me in plain words, please.
19.partnerRole: Hermano que hace preguntas claras sobre una decisión familiar y habla inglés

grammar.focus: That después de verbos como think o say introduce una idea (my conclusion is that I buy); so that expresa el propósito para quien escucha (so that it is clear).

examples.es: My provisional conclusion is that I buy the used car.
examples.en: Mi conclusión provisional es que compro el auto usado.

examples.es: Explain the alternative so that it is clear.
examples.en: Explícame la alternativa para que quede clara.

reading.title: A complete household case
target: Alba and Joaquin have a household case that combines a disputed transaction, a reduced income, and investment questions.
Alba: What is the status of the household case? I want to know what is still open before the end of the month.
Joaquin: Let's review the disputed transaction first. There is a duplicate charge of $240.00 on the shared card.
Alba: The bank opened an investigation, and the pending refund arrives when the merchant confirms the error.
Joaquin: When does the pending refund arrive? I need to know whether this month's budget changes.
Alba: There is a complication: the merchant only accepts $120.00 of the error, and the bank is still investigating the other $120.00.
Alba: Also, my income fell by $400.00 this month, because I had to give up overtime on the shift.
Joaquin: Then we need to adjust the budget, and the unexpected expense of $150.00 for the repair counts too.
Alba: Let's take $150.00 from the emergency fund only for the repair; the rent comes out of the charge account, as usual.
Joaquin: With $400.00 less, the revised budget covers the essential expenses if we lower the monthly contribution from $300.00 to $100.00 and cut $200.00 from eating out.
Alba: Our card payment commitment is $250.00 a month, and we write it on the family calendar.
Joaquin: What are the household priorities this year? For me, the reserve first and then the investment.
Alba: Let's prepare the questions for the adviser about the investment plan and diversification.
Joaquin: We also ask what costs the investment plan has and what happens if we need the money earlier.
Alba: We close the case when the full refund appears, and we write down the closing date of the case.
Joaquin keeps the investigation reference number, a copy of the revised budget, and the list of questions for the adviser.
Alba and Joaquin sign their payment commitment for the month and schedule the next household review.
native: Alba y Joaquín tienen un caso del hogar que combina una transacción en disputa, un ingreso reducido y preguntas de inversión.
Alba: ¿Cuál es el estado del caso del hogar? Quiero saber qué queda pendiente antes de fin de mes.
Joaquín: Revisemos primero la transacción en disputa. Hay un cargo duplicado de $240.00 en la tarjeta compartida.
Alba: El banco abrió una investigación, y el reembolso pendiente llega cuando el comercio confirme el error.
Joaquín: ¿Cuándo llega el reembolso pendiente? Necesito saber si cambia el presupuesto de este mes.
Alba: Hay una complicación: el comercio solo reconoce $120.00 del error, y el banco sigue investigando los otros $120.00.
Alba: Además, mi ingreso de este mes bajó $400.00, porque tuve que dejar las horas extra en el turno.
Joaquín: Entonces hay que ajustar el presupuesto, y el gasto imprevisto de $150.00 de la reparación también cuenta.
Alba: Tomemos $150.00 del fondo de emergencia solo para la reparación; la renta sale de la cuenta de cargo, como siempre.
Joaquín: Con $400.00 menos, el presupuesto revisado cubre los gastos esenciales si bajamos la aportación mensual de $300.00 a $100.00 y recortamos $200.00 de comida fuera.
Alba: Nuestro compromiso de pago de la tarjeta es de $250.00 al mes, y lo anotamos en el calendario familiar.
Joaquín: ¿Cuáles son las prioridades del hogar este año? Para mí, primero la reserva y después la inversión.
Alba: Preparemos las preguntas para el asesor sobre el plan de inversión y la diversificación.
Joaquín: También preguntamos qué costos tiene el plan de inversión y qué pasa si necesitamos el dinero antes.
Alba: Cerramos el caso cuando aparezca el reembolso completo, y anotamos la fecha de cierre del caso.
Joaquín guarda el número de referencia de la investigación, una copia del presupuesto revisado y la lista de preguntas para el asesor.
Alba y Joaquín firman su compromiso de pago para el mes y programan la siguiente revisión del hogar.

20.speaking: En una revisión del hogar con tu pareja, resuelve un cargo duplicado de $240.00, ajusta el presupuesto después de un mes con menos ingreso y haz la lista de preguntas de inversión para el asesor. Termina diciendo cuándo se cierra el caso, cuánto tomarás del fondo de emergencia y el compromiso de pago del mes.
20.openingLine: Hi. Let's go through the household case step by step. What is still pending?
20.partnerRole: Pareja que participa en una revisión completa del hogar y habla inglés

grammar.focus: Después de when, el inglés usa presente aunque hable del futuro (we close the case when the refund appears); el español usa subjuntivo (cuando aparezca). Had to + verbo base es una obligación pasada.

examples.es: We close the case when the refund appears.
examples.en: Cerramos el caso cuando aparezca el reembolso.

examples.es: I had to give up the overtime.
examples.en: Tuve que dejar las horas extra.
